name: perturbation-demo
title: Perturbation demo — gene knockouts and media shifts on the baseline whole cell
question: How do you apply a gene knockout or a media change to the v2ecoli baseline, minimally?

executive.what_is_this:
A minimal, self-contained demonstration of the two lightweight perturbation
levers built directly into the `baseline` composite. Both reuse the existing
ParCa cache — no re-fit — so each perturbation is a one-line variant:

  - `knockouts`: translation-level gene knockouts. Each named gene's
    translation efficiency is zeroed on the cached polypeptide-initiation
    config, so no protein is made — a functional knockout with no ParCa
    re-fit. (Folded in from the former KO_baseline composite.)
  - `media`: an in-cache media shift. The environment's initial media_id is
    set to any condition in the cache's saved_media, so the media_update step
    moves the cell onto that condition on the first tick and metabolism
    responds (e.g. amino-acid-rich media grows faster).

The single study `ko-and-media` runs the wild-type baseline against a lacY
knockout and an amino-acid-rich medium, side by side. This is a starting
point / how-to for perturbing the whole cell — not a rigorous result. For a
rigorously-calibrated media condition, run a per-condition ParCa cache
instead (see the v2ecoli-vecoli-comparison investigation's succinate study).
